title: Getting Projects Creatively Under Way: The Five Phases of Project Planning
coreMove: Move a stalled project through purpose, outcome, ideas, structure, and next physical action without turning planning into a hobby

exampleSpecs.domain: a community theater director preparing a first rehearsal for a small musical
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer director with cast members arriving next Tuesday
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether rehearsal time turns into vague enthusiasm or produces a playable first scene by the end of the week
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director starts with why the rehearsal matters, pictures the successful first week, dumps every concern onto paper, groups the concerns into rehearsal blocks, then names the next physical action: print the scene breakdown and place it on the piano bench

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospital charge nurse coordinating a weekend move to a temporary ward
exampleSpecs.audience: a charge nurse responsible for patient safety during a disruptive facilities change
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether missing supplies, unclear handoffs, or vague responsibilities create avoidable risk for patients and staff
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse refuses to treat 'move ward' as one giant task and instead defines the desired outcome, captures loose worries, sorts them into equipment, staffing, patient communication, and records, then assigns the next visible action for each live area

exampleSpecs.domain: a divorced parent planning a ninth-grade graduation weekend across two households
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent trying to make a family event calm without controlling every person involved
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the teenager experiences the weekend as supported or as another round of adult confusion and last-minute texts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the parent uses the five phases in plain language during a short call: agree on the purpose, describe what a good weekend looks like, list all logistics without judging them, organize who owns what, and leave with one next phone call and one calendar hold

exampleSpecs.domain: a sous-chef designing the rollout for a seasonal dinner special
exampleSpecs.audience: a kitchen lead balancing creativity with service constraints
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a promising dish becomes a chaotic service problem because recipe testing, sourcing, prep timing, and staff briefing were never made concrete
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the before version is a cloudy ambition to 'launch the spring dish'; the after version shows purpose, picture of a successful service, raw idea capture, grouped prep streams, and the next action of calling the fishmonger before noon

exampleSpecs.domain: a legal aid attorney preparing a tenant-rights clinic at a public library
exampleSpecs.audience: an attorney with limited time and many vulnerable clients depending on clear guidance
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether attendees leave with usable next steps or with more confusion about forms, deadlines, and rights
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the attorney separates principled constraints from logistics, visualizes the participant leaving with a completed intake path, brainstorms questions and materials freely, organizes them into clinic stations, and identifies the first physical action: draft the one-page intake flow

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school robotics coach restarting a team after a failed tournament
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher-coach trying to rebuild momentum without shaming students
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the team learns from the failure and starts building again, or stays stuck in blame and vague promises to 'work harder'
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach uses the five phases to convert regret into planning: restate the purpose of the team, picture a better competition day, collect every breakdown, sort issues into design, testing, travel, and roles, then pick the next action students can do in the shop today

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance harpist organizing a small benefit concert at a retirement home
exampleSpecs.audience: an independent musician juggling performance, venue details, donors, and travel
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the concert actually happens smoothly or remains a generous idea with no owner for invitations, equipment, repertoire, or arrival timing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the musician notices that creative projects need both imagination and closure: she lets ideas expand during brainstorming, then deliberately narrows them into categories and chooses the next physical action rather than polishing the plan
